related_questions.question: How is COVID-19 spread from person to person?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 spreads primarily through respiratory droplets and particles released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes. These droplets and particles can be inhaled by others or land on their eyes, nose, or mouth, or potentially contaminate surfaces. Even individuals without symptoms can transmit the virus.
snippet_highlighted_words: through respiratory droplets and particles released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes

list.snippet: Respiratory Droplets and Particles: When an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes, they release tiny droplets and particles containing the virus.
Inhalation: These droplets and particles can be inhaled directly by people nearby.
Surface Contamination: In some instances, these droplets and particles can land on surfaces, and people can become infected by touching these surfaces and then touching their face.
Close Contact: Close proximity to an infected individual significantly increases the risk of transmission, especially in indoor settings where the virus can linger in the air.
Asymptomatic Transmission: People can spread the virus even if they don't have symptoms.
